activity: On a live consumer-electronics production line, pick tablet parts from a conveyor, place them into test boxes and divert anomalous items; no device assembly.
objects: Tablet components, test boxes, anomalous items
reliability: >99.9% (reported); positional deviation tolerance up to 1 cm
caveats: Company and Chinese media reports; fixed standardized line and identical products. The Xinhua URL supplied in the source set did not fetch successfully; no independent intervention logs.

activity: Identify and pull open the door of a parked car inside a dealership using onboard sensors; did not handle luggage or assist a person physically.
caveats: Single company-described task demonstration, despite claims of broader dealership service.

system: Humanoid sewing robot with Ai10 sewing machine
activity: In garment-factory production trials, load and unload fabric at template sewing machines and position fabric for pocket setters; cannot run an end-to-end production flow without human involvement.
speed_vs_human: Exhibition tasks reported at 20–30% of human efficiency
reliability: 97% ply-separation success on one product/fabric type
caveats: Production trials described by company; narrow station tasks, single fabric/product for reported success rate, and human involvement remains necessary for the overall flow.

activity: Find packaged medicines on shelves, pick and package the requested items, then place the order in a pickup cabinet in robot-operated pharmacy stores.
objects: Packaged medicines and medical products, bags, pickup cabinet
caveats: Retail format is purpose-built and stocked/maintained by people; no evidence of general pharmacy work beyond product retrieval, packaging and order handoff.

activity: Insert high-voltage battery connectors into mating receptacles on a battery-pack production line.
objects: Flexible wiring-harness/high-voltage connectors and battery packs
speed_vs_human: Claimed three times a human worker's daily workload; hourly rate undisclosed
reliability: 99% task success (company claim)
caveats: Company claim; robot count, actual throughput and interventions not disclosed. Purpose-configured production task.

activity: Grip parcels from containers and place them onto sorting lines at a mail-processing center; no downstream sorting or delivery is established by this claim.
caveats: Source description is incomplete and does not report rates, reliability or intervention frequency; unmanned forklifts are separate machines and excluded.

activity: Fold clean napkins and other uniform laundry items at a fixed station for restaurant/laundry service; does not load or operate washers and dryers.
objects: Napkins, towels and other uniform linens
setting: Restaurant and laundry customer sites, including Din Tai Fung
customer: Din Tai Fung; additional customer sites reported
speed_vs_human: DYNA-1 ~0.6x human throughput; DYNA-2 reported 95 napkins/hour
reliability: DYNA-1 99.4% in 24-hour demo; DYNA-2 93% passing quality bar in customer throughput report
caveats: 24-hour uninterrupted run and success figures are company claims; initial trial site/log was undisclosed. Deployment limited to repeated clean-item folding, not broad laundry work.

activity: Clear dining tables and load dishwashers in unfamiliar Airbnb homes using a provided 3D map; separately demonstrated pulling an espresso shot on a consumer machine.
caveats: Company-reported demonstration; homes were unseen but provided a 3D map; no success rates reported.

activity: Fold laundry autonomously in unseen homes without per-home adaptation; results cover folding, not sorting, washing or putting clothes away.
reliability: 99.1% ±0.3% SE across 785 attempts (company report)
caveats: Company-reported test result; high success applies to laundry folding attempts and should not be generalized to other household skills.

activity: Autonomously plugs high-voltage connectors into battery-assembly equipment on a production line; the reported activity is connector insertion, not broader battery assembly.
setting: CATL Zhongzhou battery production base, factory line
reliability: Reported 99% success rate
caveats: News report describes deployment at scale and attributes the task and rate to the company; no independent throughput comparison reported.

activity: Clears tableware and food scraps from a household dining table, disposes of scraps, loads dishes and fragile glasses into a dishwasher, and starts it; a demonstrated home chore cycle, not a commercial food-service operation.
objects: Plates, utensils, cups, wine glasses, food scraps, dishwasher
setting: Household kitchens and dining areas, including company-claimed unfamiliar homes
speed_vs_human: ~0.5x (company says typical task speed; demo video is 5x)
caveats: Pre-commercial, beta planned for 2026; videos are company demonstrations, accelerated, and reliability/generalization are still being improved. Unseen-home capability is a company claim.

activity: Uses an espresso machine to prepare a shot of espresso autonomously; no broader meal preparation demonstrated.
caveats: Company demonstration; robot remains pre-commercial and the company says skill reliability/generalization is under active improvement.

activity: Folds a pile of socks, demonstrated folding six pairs in a row; does not demonstrate full laundry sorting, washing, or putting away clothes.
caveats: Company demonstration accelerated 5x; pre-commercial and reliability/generalization still being improved.

activity: Picks individual playing cards from a deck and deals blackjack hands onto a mock table at a trade-show booth; does not demonstrate casino-speed play or operation at a live casino table.
speed_vs_human: Far below casino play speed (qualitative reports)
caveats: Mock trade-show activity; press observers described dealing as extremely slow.

developer: Shenzhen Honor Smart Technology Development Co., Ltd.
activity: Completes a 21.1 km half-marathon course by autonomous navigation on a closed road course; this demonstrates endurance locomotion, not general outdoor navigation in arbitrary conditions.
speed_vs_human: 50:26 course time (faster than human world record, per report)
caveats: Organized race on a closed course; result does not establish performance on unstructured routes.

system: RB-KAIROS+ mobile manipulator with measurement probe and inspection sensors
activity: Autonomously navigates around aircraft horizontal-tail-plane skins and records stringer, flange, and thickness measurements, then generates traceable inspection data; no repair or assembly work.
objects: Aircraft horizontal tail-plane skins and structural features
caveats: Robotnik case study; measurements use predefined plans and a contact probe for referencing, but the plant needs no floor markings or structural modification.

activity: Profiles vehicle bodywork and applies soaps, waxes, and other treatments along planned trajectories, including finishing passes; does not connect or couple hoses.
caveats: Pilot research project; the source describes target applications and capabilities but provides no measured throughput or completed-cycle reliability.

activity: Runs pre-programmed routines to lead group exercise, bingo, and sing-along sessions with residents with dementia; it does not provide physical care or rehabilitation assistance.
objects: Group of elderly residents; exercise and bingo activities
setting: The Salvation Army Peacehaven Jade Circle Arena, Singapore
caveats: Pre-programmed facilitation routines, not adaptive clinical care; nursing-home staff are present.

activity: Autonomously navigates a live construction site to capture 360-degree imagery and produce progress reports for health-and-safety monitoring; performs no physical construction or material installation.
objects: Construction site and visual progress/safety conditions
caveats: Company calls this a trial; expected savings are an estimate of 40 staff-hours per month, not an independently measured result.

developer: UBTECH Robotics (at SANY Renewable Energy smart factory)
activity: Removes bolt sleeves, sorts bolts onto conveyors, transfers full trays to storage racks, and retrieves empty trays while working alongside factory staff; does not perform unspecified downstream assembly.
objects: Bolt sleeves, bolts, conveyors, full and empty trays
caveats: Company-reported factory application; ongoing duration and independent performance measures are not provided.

activity: Performs visual quality inspection of partially or fully assembled modules on moving automotive production lines; does not perform repairs or full vehicle testing.
reliability: Company reports accuracy above 99%
caveats: Capability and accuracy are company-reported; the source describes factory deployments but gives no independent validation or throughput comparison.

activity: Autonomously removes its depleted battery module and inserts a charged replacement at a swap station; this is robot self-maintenance, not a customer job task.
objects: Robot battery module and swap station
caveats: Company demonstration; the swap station is purpose-built.

activity: Perform a choreographed Yangko folk-dance number, including spinning handkerchiefs, alongside human dancers on a live broadcast stage; choreography was designed and rehearsed beforehand.
caveats: Single highly choreographed performance after months of engineer-led preparation; not improvised or reactive dancing.

activity: Perform synchronized pop-concert choreography, including flips, as backup dancers alongside a human performer; does not interact with the audience or adapt the choreography in real time.
caveats: One live entertainment performance; choreography was derived from captured human motion and pre-engineered, despite reported onboard synchronization and collision avoidance.

activity: Perform a synchronized martial-arts and acrobatics routine, including formation changes and flips, on a live broadcast stage alongside human performers; the routine is choreographed rather than combat or unscripted interaction.
caveats: Highly rehearsed performance; company and press describe it as autonomous, with no teleoperation during the routine.

activity: Perform a preprogrammed synchronized routine in formation outdoors, localizing on a cleared plaza; no manipulation or interaction with passers-by.
setting: Cleared plaza at Beijing's Temple of Heaven
caveats: Cleared, controlled performance space; trajectories were distributed by a control station, without remote manual control.

activity: Picks self-tapping nuts from a feeder and tightens them at a fixed automotive workstation during a three-hour autonomous run; task is station-specific fastening, not general assembly-line work.
setting: EV factory die-casting/assembly workshop, fixed workstation
reliability: 90.2% success (reported)
caveats: Factory trial at a fixed engineered station; performance figures are reported by Xiaomi and are below perfect reliability.

activity: Uses 3D perception and force/torque feedback to locate wrinkles and reduce them with an unmodified household iron on an ironing board; does not iron at production speed or quality.
caveats: Laboratory research demonstration on a small set of simple garments; a human places the garments on the board.

developer: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid / Universidad de Málaga, with Hospital Virgen del Rocío
activity: Leads non-contact upper-limb pose exercises and observes the patient's movements for assessment; it neither touches nor physically supports the patient.
caveats: Research evaluation with staff supervision; non-contact exercise only, not hands-on rehabilitation.

activity: Perceives, plans, changes tools, and removes multiple types of bolts from end-of-life EV battery packs; does not diagnose faults, replace components, reassemble, or test repaired packs.
objects: Bolted EV battery packs and fasteners
reliability: 98.78% bolt-removal success reported
caveats: Research platform and controlled battery-disassembly setting; reported result covers fastener removal only.

activity: Operated a consumer Keurig capsule coffee machine end to end: loaded a pod, closed the hatch and pressed brew; did not prepare or serve the coffee.
caveats: Single company video demonstration; press coverage says policy learned from about 10 hours of human video and could self-correct. No throughput or reliability data.

activity: Picked sheet-metal parts from racks or logistics containers and placed them into a welding fixture in BMW's body shop; did not perform broader assembly, welding, diagnosis or repair.
setting: BMW Plant Spartanburg body shop, active automotive production line
reliability: Target was >99% placement accuracy per shift; achieved accuracy and intervention counts not disclosed
caveats: Retrospectively reported 11-month project with about six months of daily active-line runtime; 90,000+ parts over 1,250+ runtime hours and production of 30,000+ X3s. One robot worked at a time; task remained a single repetitive placement chore. Accuracy and interventions were not reported.

activity: Picked mixed packages from a conveyor, reoriented them so barcodes faced a scanner, and returned them to the conveyor; handled boxes, poly bags and flat envelopes, but did not sort to destinations or apply labels.
objects: Rigid parcels, poly bags, flat envelopes
setting: Figure logistics workcell and conveyor at its own facility
reliability: ~95% correct barcode orientation in company evaluation
caveats: Company evaluation, not a customer shift; reported metrics and uninterrupted video are company claims.

activity: Picked up unfamiliar household objects in response to language commands; the demonstration establishes object grasping, not completion of household chores or reliable operation across homes.
caveats: Company says it can grasp 'virtually any' novel household object; this is a broad company claim, not a reported success rate or independent evaluation.

activity: Picked mixed parcels from a conveyor, read/used their barcodes to orient labels toward a scanner, and placed them back on a conveyor; did not perform downstream parcel routing or delivery.
objects: Packages including boxes, poly bags and flat envelopes
setting: Figure's Sunnyvale facility, conveyor sorting station
speed_vs_human: ~2.83 s/package in a 10-hour contest; ~98.5% of one human participant's shift output
caveats: Company-facility demonstrations, not customer deployment. The rotating fleet sorted 249,560 packages over 200 hours; errors including dropped or mis-oriented packages were visible, and intervention counts were not published. The 200-hour run was not a single robot's uninterrupted shift.

activity: Walked through a full-sized kitchen, unloaded a dishwasher, put dishes away, reloaded it and started the cycle; did not demonstrate complete kitchen cleanup or operation of other appliances.
caveats: Four-minute run with 61 sequenced loco-manipulation actions and no resets or human intervention; policy trained on data from the evaluation environment. No success rate reported.

activity: Performed separate long-horizon household tasks zero-shot in unseen homes: tidied living rooms, folded towels, and made beds; these were evaluated as distinct task types, not a combined home-cleaning service.
setting: 30 unseen Bay Area homes with unseen objects
reliability: 56% full-task success across tasks/homes (no partial credit)
caveats: Company-reported result; 56% is aggregate full-task success. Same model without Index pretraining scored 9%; comparison is not an independent evaluation.

system: π0 family (mobile manipulator and bimanual platforms)
activity: After task-specific fine-tuning, carried out multi-stage laundry folding and table bussing sequences lasting 5–20 minutes; demonstrations were bounded tasks, not general household service.
caveats: Fine-tuned for the tasks; the long sequences demonstrate task execution, not unattended household operation.

activity: Performed multi-stage kitchen and bedroom cleaning in three real homes absent from training; scope was the demonstrated cleaning sequences, not general home maintenance.
objects: Household items, kitchen and bedroom surfaces
setting: Three real homes not seen in training
caveats: The reported real-home evaluation covered three test homes; unseen mock-home results are separate from this entry.

activity: Prepared espresso drinks using a commercial espresso machine for a continuous 13-hour reported run; this was a bounded beverage-making activity, not full café operation.
objects: Espresso machine, cups and coffee ingredients
caveats: Company/researcher-reported run; the claim does not establish commercial service or human-equivalent throughput.

activity: Folded novel laundry in a new home for over two hours without interruption; no broader household chores are included.
caveats: Researcher-reported uninterrupted run; not a measure of ordinary household reliability.

activity: Executed open-ended three-to-six-step instruction sequences in kitchens and bedrooms not seen during training, including operating an espresso machine; the demonstrations do not establish broad home-service coverage.
objects: Kitchen and bedroom household objects; espresso machine
setting: Four unseen kitchens and two unseen bedrooms
reliability: Authors report 60–80% on unseen tasks or task-robot combinations; seen tasks often exceed 90%.
caveats: Reported rates are from the authors; different task and environment subsets have different success rates.

activity: Wiped a countertop and scrubbed a greasy pan with a sponge at fixed bimanual arm stations; this covers wet-cleaning subtasks, not complete kitchen cleaning.
objects: Countertop, greasy pan, sponge and cleaning cloth
caveats: Company challenge demonstrations, described as initial solutions rather than production-reliable behavior.

activity: Performed cooking demonstrations including sautéing shrimp using a mobile bimanual robot; the reported recipe tasks required roughly 50 demonstrations in the target environment and did not amount to autonomous meal service.
caveats: Task-specific demonstrations and substantial in-environment demonstrations were required.

system: HomeBody with Unitree G1 and GPT-6 Astra
activity: Explored an unfamiliar kitchen, built a digital twin and spatial memory, then tidied objects and fetched items from drawers using a skill library; this did not demonstrate general-purpose home upkeep.
objects: Kitchen items, drawers and household surfaces
caveats: No success rate reported; authors noted latency, finger-servo overheating and high compute costs.

activity: Roamed Google office buildings, found waste stations and moved discarded items between recycling, compost and landfill bins; it did not empty bins or transport waste to collection areas.
objects: Light office waste including cans, bottles, paper cups and cardboard containers
setting: Three Google office buildings, 30 waste stations
reliability: Final system sorted about 84% of objects correctly in evaluation; real deployments reduced bin contamination 40–50% by weight.
caveats: 23-robot research deployment over two years; not a paid product or routine commercial service.

system: Everyday Robots mobile manipulator with learned wiping policy
activity: Used a wiping tool and whole-body motion to clean crumbs and liquid spills from tables; no complete custodial workflow was demonstrated.
objects: Table surfaces, crumbs and liquid spills
setting: Indoor tables in laboratory and Google office contexts
caveats: Real-hardware validation; constrained indoor tables and wiping task.

system: PaLM-SayCan on Everyday Robots mobile manipulator
activity: Interpreted a spoken request and fetched a requested item from an office micro-kitchen; this was item retrieval, not general kitchen work.
objects: Food and drink items and kitchen objects
reliability: Approximately three-quarters end-to-end success, as summarized by the cited source.
caveats: A bounded set of fetch requests in a known workplace setting.

activity: Flattened a shirt, retrieved a hanger from a rack, inserted it into the shirt collar and hung the shirt back on the rack using bimanual arms; did not dress a person or manage a laundry workflow.
setting: Fixed tabletop bimanual workcell with rack
reliability: 75% on easy variant; 70% on messy variant.
caveats: Fixed workcell; success rates reported for experimental variants.

activity: Tied a shoelace using a learned bimanual policy at a fixed tabletop workstation; did not dress or lace a shoe in a human-use workflow.
caveats: Research task, not a production process.

activity: Removed a replaceable finger from a robot hand and inserted a replacement finger; this was a single trained part swap, not diagnosis or general robot repair.
objects: Robot gripper finger and replacement part
reliability: 75% over 20 trials per the cited summary.
caveats: A narrowly trained maintenance subtask; not general repair.

activity: Folded a sheet of paper into an origami fox from instruction, carrying out multiple alignment, bending, pinching and creasing actions; this did not demonstrate broader paper-craft production.
caveats: Research demonstration on a fixed bimanual platform.

system: Gemini Robotics 1.5 on ALOHA-class bimanual arms
activity: Sorted clothing by color and packed clothes into a suitcase from instructions; did not search luggage for concealed items or perform full travel packing independently.
caveats: Research demonstrations; fixed lab platform.

developer: AIST (Japan National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology)
activity: Separated a gypsum board from a stack, carried and positioned it against a wall frame, then picked up a screwdriver and fastened the board to the frame; did not perform full construction work.
setting: Purpose-built residential construction mock-up in laboratory
caveats: Slow laboratory demonstration; no jobsite deployment.

activity: Slid a hand beneath a supine mannequin's back and assisted a supine-to-raised transition; this was a sub-step and did not include full repositioning with padding or stabilization.
caveats: Mannequin demonstration, not patient care.

system: ORB (Operating Room Bot), Fetch mobile manipulator
activity: Retrieved individual operating-room supplies and restocked their locations in a mock supply room; did not stock a live operating room or handle clinical procedures.
reliability: 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success in laboratory experiments.
caveats: Research prototype; reported success is below unattended clinical stocking requirements.

developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotic Caregiving and Human Interaction Lab
system: SkinGrip soft manipulator on Hello Robot Stretch RE1
activity: Wiped shaving cream from participants' arms and legs with a soft, sensorized manipulator; the demonstration did not include face washing or full bathing.
objects: Human limbs, shaving cream and wiping tool
setting: Hospital bed with limb secured in a purpose-built holder
caveats: Twelve able-bodied participants; shaving cream represented soil; constrained limb positioning.

system: RoBE / Bodies Uncovered bedding manipulation system
activity: Manipulated a blanket over a supine person while adapting to body pose and blanket configuration; did not demonstrate full bed-making or dressing assistance.
objects: Blanket and person lying in bed
caveats: Validated with 12 participants in a laboratory setting.

developer: Carnegie Mellon RoboTouch Lab / Toyota Research Institute
system: Perceptive batter stirring and pouring research robot
activity: Mixed flour and water to a target uniformity, estimated mixture ratio and level by haptic sensing, and poured the viscous batter into specified shapes; not full food preparation.
caveats: Single laboratory food-manipulation workflow.

system: Twin KUKA KMR iiwa mobile robotic chemists
activity: Moved and handled chemical samples among an automated synthesis platform, UPLC-MS and benchtop NMR, operated the instruments and used analysis results to select follow-up reactions in an exploratory chemistry workflow; not general laboratory work.
objects: Chemical samples, vials and laboratory instruments
setting: Working university synthesis laboratory shared with human researchers
caveats: Specialized equipment and a defined synthesis-analysis workflow in one laboratory.

activity: Perceived and removed multiple types of bolts from end-of-life EV battery packs; did not dismantle or reinstall complete powertrain components or handle attached wiring and lines.
objects: Bolts and used EV battery packs
reliability: 98.78% reported bolt-removal success.
caveats: Research prototype; demonstrated bolt-removal subtask only.

system: From Pixels to Shelf mobile manipulator (Stretch 3)
activity: Picked products from stock and placed/fronted them on supermarket shelves in a lab replica; did not stock a live operating supermarket.
reliability: Over 98% pick-and-place success across 724 events.
caveats: Authors report cost and performance remain inferior to human workers; laboratory replica only.

activity: Prepare espresso drinks end-to-end at a fixed professional coffee workstation, including grinding, machine operation, pouring and wiping the machine; not general café service or customer interaction.
objects: Coffee beans, espresso machine and portafilter, cups, milk, cloth towel
reliability: >90% success per stage (company-reported)
caveats: Company-reported all-day run (5:30am–11:30pm); fixed workstation and prescribed task. Throughput and reliability figures are company-reported; interventions/corrections were used during training, not claimed during the evaluation run.

activity: Fold and assemble flattened cardboard boxes, recover from folding errors or stuck-together blanks, and apply labels for factory chocolate packaging; not packing the boxes with product or operating a whole packaging line.
caveats: Company demonstration reports 59 boxes; factory-use boxes, but this is not evidence of routine customer deployment.

activity: Fold diverse, novel laundry items into stacks in a real home over an extended run; not a complete laundry service including sorting, washing or drying.
caveats: Company reports folding 50 novel items for hours without interruption; this is a demo, not routine laundry service.

activity: Fold garments from a hamper by grasping, flattening and stacking them; not a complete laundry workflow.
caveats: Research demonstration on a controlled setup; the cited claims also mention mobile-robot variants, but this entry describes the fixed-arm setup.

activity: Clear a laboratory table by sorting dishes, cups and cutlery into a bussing bin and trash into a waste bin; not service in an operating dining room or dishwashing.
objects: Dishes, cups, cutlery, food waste and trash, bussing and waste bins
reliability: 0.875 on the 'Bussing Hard' evaluation (reported in cited claim)
caveats: Fine-tuned lab benchmark with bins placed beside the table; not a customer deployment.

activity: Set a table by taking a placemat, dishes, silverware, napkin and cup from a bin and arranging them on a table according to language instructions; not full dining-room setup or meal service.
objects: Placemat, dishes, silverware, napkin, cup, storage bin
caveats: Controlled lab evaluation; task scope is arranging the listed tableware, not a complete hospitality service.

activity: Perform multi-step household tidying in kitchens and bedrooms: pick up everyday items, put dishes in a sink and objects/clothing in drawers or baskets, and wipe spills; not cooking, dishwashing or a reliable full-home cleaning service.
objects: Household clutter, dishes, clothing, drawers, baskets, sink, sponge/cloth
setting: Real homes, including homes not seen during training
reliability: Partial success; often makes errors (developer-reported)
caveats: Research demonstrations in unseen homes; developers explicitly describe limitations and frequent errors.

activity: Prepare a shrimp dish by adding oil, adding and flipping shrimp in a pan, and plating it; not a complete meal or kitchen shift.
reliability: 40% whole-task success in 5 trials (paper)
caveats: Single 75-second cooking task after 20 demonstrations; small evaluation set and low whole-task success.

activity: Clean spilled wine from a table by fetching a towel, lifting a glass, wiping the spill and replacing the glass; not general-purpose room cleaning.
reliability: 95% whole-task success with co-training (paper; 20 trials)
caveats: Imitation-learned task from 50 demonstrations, evaluated in a controlled setup.

activity: Push a row of chairs into position in front of a desk, including chairs not used in demonstrations; not furniture moving throughout a building.
reliability: 80% whole-task success with co-training (paper; 20 trials)
caveats: Controlled experiment using 50 demonstrations; evaluates a specific row of chairs and desk.

activity: Navigate a lobby, press an elevator call button and enter the elevator; not autonomous elevator operation or travel between floors.
reliability: 95% whole-task success with co-training (paper; 20 trials)
caveats: Research task in a controlled building-like setup; entering the lift is the end of the task.

activity: Run a closed-loop photocatalyst experiment campaign: move vials between stations, weigh and dispense reagents, prepare and process samples, measure hydrogen production, and use Bayesian optimization to select subsequent mixtures; not general laboratory work or independent instrument repair.
objects: Reagents, sample vials and racks, laboratory dispensers, photoreactor, gas chromatograph
reliability: 688 experiments over eight days; sixfold photocatalyst activity improvement reported
caveats: Laboratory was otherwise largely unmodified but had purpose-installed stations, positioning markers and custom workflow equipment; human intervention was limited but not absent across the whole campaign.

system: Autonomous mobile robotic chemists (KUKA mobile manipulators)
activity: Carry samples between an automated synthesis platform and shared UPLC-MS/NMR instruments, collect measurements and apply predefined criteria to select reactions for replication, scale-up or further synthesis; not choosing the research question or replacing expert chemical judgment.
objects: Reaction samples, vials and racks, synthesis platform, UPLC-MS and benchtop NMR
caveats: Almost four days of operation with chemical/consumable restocking by researchers; experiments and decision thresholds were selected by experts beforehand, and unexpected products still required human interpretation.

activity: Locate a control panel in a challenge arena, identify and grasp the correct wrench, and use it to rotate a valve stem; not general maintenance or work on arbitrary industrial valves.
caveats: Competition demonstration with a prepared challenge panel and specified tool.

activity: Recognize a person approaching, stop while moving around a kitchen island, high-five them and resume only after they leave the robot's path; not general social interaction or safety assistance.
reliability: 85% whole-task success with co-training (paper; 20 trials)
caveats: Controlled study with unseen people and clothing; narrow interaction task.

system: Autonomous button-pressing mobile manipulator (Wang and Hauser)
activity: Detect a control panel, position the mobile base and press buttons or switches using a compliant fingertip; not operating complex machinery or repairing controls.
caveats: Research demonstration of selected control panels; not broad manipulation of arbitrary controls.

developer: University of Groningen / University Medical Center Groningen
activity: Administer auditory psychophysical tests by presenting sounds and recording participant responses; not examination of ears or clinical diagnosis.
caveats: Interface-based research study with normal-hearing adults; no physical examination or diagnosis.

activity: Deliver instructions and in-test feedback during automated visual-field perimetry while the perimeter measures patient responses; not independent eye diagnosis or treatment.
objects: Patient, visual-field perimeter and test interface
reliability: Measured sensitivity and reliability indices were not significantly different from in-person operator feedback in the study
caveats: Scripted verbal instruction and feedback; study involved 40 adults and does not establish broad clinical autonomy.

developer: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid / Columbia University
activity: Plan and execute ironing strokes with a hand iron on cloth spread approximately flat on a surface; not ironing hanging garments or producing commercial finish quality.
caveats: Lab demonstration on approximately flattened fabric; not a complete garment-care workflow.

activity: Spread a cloth over a desk as a table covering and place a basket on it; not routine table setting or broad fabric handling.
caveats: Single integrated laboratory experiment.

system: Mobile robotic process chemist (KUKA mobile manipulator)
activity: Move between fixed fume-hood stations to charge a reactor, perform process-scale chemical synthesis and work-up, and analyze the products; not general-purpose chemistry in arbitrary lab layouts.
objects: Reagents, 1 L reactor, balance, filtration equipment and UHPLC-MS
caveats: Preprint-era demonstration; equipment fixed in saved locations, with purpose-built dispensing devices.

activity: Demonstrate and verbally supervise prescribed stretching exercises for people with chronic low back pain; not hands-on assistance, clinical monitoring or individualized physiotherapy.
caveats: Feasibility trial found current robot supervision not feasible for physical-activity sessions; adherence and usability were concerns.

activity: Use visual and haptic feedback to approach and open doors in varied, previously unseen settings; not fitting locks, modifying doors or completing work on door hardware.
reliability: About 90% success on the opening action (source summary)
caveats: Success applies to the door-opening action in research tests, not broad building operations.

activity: Moves standardized totes from autonomous mobile robots to conveyors, and stacks totes at designated floor locations, in a working fulfillment warehouse; does not pick individual inventory items or perform open-ended order packing.
setting: GXO Flowery Branch fulfillment warehouse, Georgia
reliability: Over 100,000 totes moved; approximately 98% on-task accuracy per company claim
caveats: Company/customer deployment claims; fixed, repetitive workflow and standardized objects. Human-occupied warehouse; intervention counts and throughput not stated.

activity: Transfers 25-pound baskets of bearing components from a stamping press to an industrial washing machine during production shifts inside a safety cage; does not work openly among staff.
setting: Schaeffler bearings plant, Cheraw, South Carolina
caveats: Source reports eight hours/day over two shifts with recharge break; no throughput or intervention statistics. Operates alone behind Plexiglas guarding.

activity: Completes putwall automation work autonomously in real facilities on a continuous basis; specific object flow and site are not disclosed, so this is distinct from the documented GXO tote workflow only at the level of the reported putwall task.
reliability: 97% success rate (company claim)
caveats: Company claim; exact site, run length, task details, and intervention counts undisclosed.

activity: Uses vision to locate fixtures and engine covers, then moves bulky automotive engine covers between supplier containers and sequences a dolly in an industrial cell; does not assemble or install the parts on a vehicle.
objects: Bulky automotive engine covers, supplier containers, dolly
caveats: Developer demonstration; supplied bin-location list and industrial cell setup.

system: Spot with Spot Arm and Autowalk
activity: Opens doors as part of autonomous, scheduled industrial inspection missions; autonomous arm manipulation is limited to this constrained door-opening action, not general equipment servicing.
caveats: Door opening described as beta/available to beta customers; other arm work requires operator direction.

activity: On a high-level command, trips and racks out one known 600 V circuit breaker in a switchgear room; does not meter, diagnose faults, or repair equipment.
objects: 600 V circuit breaker and switchgear cabinet
caveats: Custom end effector and pre-engineered procedure at a known cabinet; human provides high-level command from a safe distance.

system: Physical AI on industrial robot hardware
activity: Detects, tracks, aligns, and inserts flexible wire connectors into targets moving on a conveyor at a Tier 1 automotive supplier; the reported activity is connector mating, not a full assembly process.
objects: Flexible wire assemblies and moving connector targets
setting: Automotive supplier production conveyor / industrial cell
reliability: >99.5% task success; 2.54-second cycle (company claim)
